payload.name: Verify temporal, ordinal, and explicit-claim evidence
payload.description: Retrieve when a question includes a specific date/period, relative time, ordinal (e.g., 'third screenplay'), or a claim/help/suggestion whose exact topic/predicate may be missing from initial evidence; use when candidates are temporally mismatched, or a future-plan/interest memory is the only 'evidence'.
content: Check each candidate memory's world_start/world_end: for a named date, require world_start <= target <= world_end (or null end); reject memories from other dates and keep searching if needed.
For approximate-date questions, relax or widen the time filter (e.g., ±3 months) when the subject/action match is strong; apply strict filtering only for explicit interval questions.
For after-event/next-action questions, search memories of the same subject with the same or adjacent world_start timestamps, or inspect other versions from the same source/turn.

For completion-date questions, use completion/creation synonyms and relative-time qualifiers ('completed a few days ago'); do not substitute a publication/exhibit date, and compute the date from the memory's reference time.

For ordinals, do not pick the most similar title; search completion/achievement phrasing ('completed', 'finished', 'wrote', 'achievement') and require the memory to link the work to the ordinal or be the only possible match.

For vague help/suggestion/claim evidence, never answer with a guessed topic/predicate absent from retrieved text; run a follow-up targeted search (e.g., '<name> struggling with', '<name> suggested <item>') and require explicit verbatim or clear-paraphrase support.

payload.name: Decompose multi-facet questions and enumerate all expected entities
payload.description: Retrieve when a question asks about multiple named people/entities, multiple constraints/facets, or an exhaustive list (e.g., 'What does X do besides Y?', 'What games does X play?', 'Who in X's family...?'), especially when the first search covers only one facet/person/item.
content: Identify every named subject, constraint, and expected list item; the final answer must include at least one supporting memory for each facet and entity.

After the combined search, check coverage per facet/entity. If any is missing, run targeted searches pairing that name with the property/activity keywords (e.g., 'Deborah time management', 'Evan son injury'), trying multiple phrasings.

For 'besides/other than' questions, run a broad search with only the person's name and activity/hobby terms, and enumerate via structured predicates 'activity', 'hobby', 'interest', 'routine' across event/profile/state memories.

For enumeration/list questions, use activity verbs ('playing', 'won', 'recommended', 'watched') and category keywords; probe with named-entity templates like '[person] played [game]' and tolerate spelling variants.

For 'who' questions about groups, enumerate possible members via relationship terms (son, spouse, parent, sibling) and search each member with the event/attribute; increase top_k or use structured filters until all supported persons are found.

Do not finalize an enumeration or multi-subject answer until every expected facet/entity has support; if one genuinely has none, say that part is unavailable rather than substituting another subject's information.

payload.name: Lexical and memory-kind expansion for under-retrieved queries
payload.description: Retrieve when initial search returns no or weak results for a question about preferences, current activities, plans, counts, mottoes, locations, or attribute lists, or when results are dominated by off-topic/topical memories and miss an explicit statement with different wording, memory kind, or predicate.
content: If the first hybrid/keyword search misses a relevant memory, do not answer 'No information available.' Rerun with at least one semantic/hybrid query using the full question and one keyword query expanded with synonyms, inflections, and associated terms (e.g., 'rejected'->'rejection', 'script'->'screenplay', 'motto'->'saying/sign/symbol', 'snow'->'winter/sunny/prefer', 'location'->'spot/nearby/area').

Do not restrict memory_kind to a single type: for current-activity questions include 'event' and 'state'; for plans include 'event', 'plan', and 'goal'; for lists/favorites include 'preference'; otherwise omit the filter.

Add predicate-targeted queries such as '<subject> misses <object>', '<subject> enjoys <category>', '<subject> has active project', or '<subject> completed <work>', and inspect returned memories for paraphrase language even if the exact query word is absent.
For 'where' questions, expand with location-synonym keywords combined with the subject and activity verb, and prefer a location-bearing memory over a future-plan or activity-only memory.
Prefer explicit preference/state memories over events/plans that only imply the answer, and continue searching until you have a memory that names the requested entity or answers the question.
